solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Top-quality ball game by sailor

parts.note: fives is a British court game in which a ball is struck with the gloved hand
tar is an old slang word for a seaman

explanation.surface: A sporting report praising a superb match played by a navy man.
explanation.walkthrough: FIVES is a British game, rather like squash played with the hand instead of a racket.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-star hotel or review is the highest grade, so the phrase means of the best quality.

clue.text: Fine deed, in truth

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
a deed is an act, something done

explanation.surface: A solemn affirmation that some good action really happened.
explanation.definitionFit: Something true is a matter of reality; a single true statement is a piece of that reality.

clue.text: Stage performer unfortunately quits in revolt

indicators.note: something gone unfortunately has gone wrong, so the letters of the following words are put out of order

explanation.surface: An actor sadly walks out of the show in protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges all thirteen letters of QUITS IN REVOLT.
explanation.definitionFit: A ventriloquist is an entertainer on stage who throws the voice into a dummy.

clue.text: Unapproachable, like a rugby half-back?

parts.note: the stand-off, or fly-half, is one of the two half-backs in a rugby team
the suffix -ish means rather like, as in boyish

explanation.surface: A rugby player at half-back is aloof, keeping his distance from everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby the stand-off (fly-half) is the half-back who stands away from the scrum; the question mark flags the playful split of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof and cold keeps others at arm's length, so is hard to approach.

clue.text: An endless boring task to be a TV presenter

indicators.note: without its end means the final letter of the word for the task is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a tedious routine job

explanation.surface: Being a television host is a never-ending tedious job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the final E of CHORE, leaving CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A news anchor is the main presenter who holds a broadcast together, linking reports.

clue.text: Detached area? I'll say!

indicators.note: say signals that the clue words are to be spoken and the spelling taken from their sound

parts.note: the contraction of I will, pronounced like the word for a small island

explanation.surface: An exclamation of emphatic agreement about some remote spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll say!' looks like an exclamation of agreement; 'say' is the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An island is land cut off by water, so a playful description of it is a separated patch of ground.

clue.text: Cost of attending church wedding? It should go to the staff

definitions.meaning: whimsically, the fee for a religious service in church

definitions.text: It should go to the staff
definitions.meaning: a restaurant's added percentage on the bill, meant for waiters

explanation.definitionFit: Restaurants add a percentage to bills as a tip for waiters; read literally, the words mean a fee for a church ceremony.

clue.text: Plea to add two points to formal agreement

parts.note: E and N are the compass points east and north
a treaty is a formally concluded agreement between states

explanation.surface: A request to append a couple of clauses to a signed agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest request or appeal, the same as a plea.

clue.text: A line dance?

parts.note: seems to mean a modern country-style routine, but describes the party dance done in a long snaking single file

explanation.definitionFit: In this Latin American party dance people hold the person in front and form a long chain.

clue.text: Spiteful type hosting scanty entertainment

indicators.note: one word hosting another holds it inside like a guest

parts.note: a cat is a catty, spiteful person
bare means meagre, scanty

explanation.surface: A malicious person putting on a skimpy, risqué show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hosting' reads as staging the show, but signals a container: the catty type takes the scanty word in.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a nightclub or restaurant show of songs and comedy, a form of entertainment.

clue.text: Supporter holding seat is no minister

indicators.note: holding means the first word contains the second within it

parts.note: a backer is someone who supports or funds
a bench is a long seat

explanation.surface: A political ally keeping his parliamentary seat is not in government.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' signals a container. In Britain a backbencher is an MP holding no government or shadow post, seated behind the front benches.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of Parliament without office sit on the rear benches, so are not government ministers.

clue.text: Broadcaster busy emitting dangerous material

parts.note: radio is a broadcasting medium
active means busy, occupied

explanation.surface: A busy broadcaster pumping out harmful content.
explanation.definitionFit: Radioactive substances give off ionising radiation, which is harmful to living things.

clue.text: See bully wounded: good shot!

indicators.note: something wounded is damaged, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Look, the playground tormentor has been hit: well aimed!
explanation.definitionFit: Hitting the centre of a dartboard or target is the best possible shot, used as a cry of praise.

clue.text: Pitiful, heartless, corrupt? Here's a boost

indicators.note: something corrupt has been distorted, so the remaining letters are scrambled
without its heart means the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: A list of insults, followed by an offer of encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' takes the middle I from PITIFUL, leaving PITFUL; 'corrupt' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift in spirits or morale is an encouraging boost.

clue.text: A tendency to keep son away

indicators.note: keep means hold inside, so the one word retains the other within it

parts.note: a bent is a natural inclination
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A parent's inclination to keep their boy from home.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone absent is not present, gone elsewhere.

clue.text: Illegally dump end of tiny antenna?

definitions.meaning: to discard rubbish unlawfully at the roadside, a British term
playfully, the point at the extremity of an insect's feeler, an insect being a small winged creature

explanation.walkthrough: Fly-tipping is British for dumping rubbish illegally; the second reading splits it as the tip of a fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly-tipping is dumping waste on land without permission; the second sense reads it as the point of an insect's feeler.

clue.text: £51 meal, one omitting the food?

parts.note: LI is 51 in Roman numerals
a quid is British slang for one pound sterling
lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: A pricey midday meal at which nobody actually eats.
explanation.walkthrough: Quid is British slang for a pound; 51 in Roman numerals comes first in the answer. A liquid lunch is a midday session of drinking instead of eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A drinking session taking the place of a midday meal skips anything solid to eat.

clue.text: Depend entirely? Only half

indicators.note: only half of the word is used, here its second four letters

explanation.surface: A question about total dependence, answered that it is only partial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Only half' takes the back half of ENTIRELY.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to trust and depend upon them.

clue.text: Record one article: time for a descriptive word

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
I is the Roman numeral one
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A recording, a piece of writing, and the moment to choose an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An epithet is an adjective or phrase characterising someone, such as 'the Great'.

clue.text: A multitude in store, it's said

indicators.note: it's said indicates the word is chosen for how it is spoken, not its spelling

parts.note: a hoard is a stockpile or store

explanation.surface: Reports of a crowd of people packed into a shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop, but it is a stockpile, HOARD, spoken the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A horde is a large crowd or throng.

clue.text: Food deposited in meat-safe

indicators.note: deposited in means the letters are lodged within the following word

explanation.surface: Provisions stored away in a ventilated cupboard for meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposited in' marks the run of letters inside MEAT-SAFE. A meat-safe is an old-fashioned mesh cupboard for keeping meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal for food, as in 'the eats were good'.

clue.text: Press lay about, spread so thinly?

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Journalists lay around, scattered too thin to be useful.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparsely means thinly or meagrely distributed, with gaps between the items.
